accuracyFlags.claim: Section 09: refusing the breath screening test 'is an offence in its own right and is treated more seriously than a positive result' (also the 'Refusing is worse than failing' callout).
accuracyFlags.correct: Refusing a roadside breath screening test is not itself an offence (Land Transport Act 1998 s 68-69): refusal lets police require an evidential breath or blood test. Failing to accompany the officer or remain (s 59) carries up to $4,500 and possible disqualification; refusing a blood test (s 60) carries up to 3 months' prison or $4,500 plus at least 6 months' disqualification, the same as being over 400 mcg/L (s 56(1)) and harsher than the 251-400 mcg/L infringement band (s 56(1A)). Suggested: 'You can be required to take a screening test at any time. If you refuse, police will require you to come for an evidential breath or blood test. Refusing the blood test is a criminal offence with the same penalties as serious drink driving, so refusing gains you nothing.'

accuracyFlags.claim: Section 06: 'fatigue is a factor in a substantial share of visitor crashes here. The first 48 hours after arrival are the highest risk period of the whole trip.'
accuracyFlags.correct: Unsupported and contradicted: the Ministry of Transport's 'Overseas Drivers in Crashes' (2016) found very few short-term visitors crash in their first few days and fatigue is generally not a contributing factor; overseas licence holders are in under 6% of fatal and injury crashes. Remove the statistical claims or reword as general advice ('a long-haul flight and jet lag add to fatigue, so keep arrival day short').
accuracyFlags.source: Ministry of Transport 'Overseas Drivers in Crashes' (2016), as quoted in Associate Transport Minister Craig Foss's release: https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2016/04/foreign-driver-myths-debunked-by-report---foss.html ; https://autotalk.co.nz/?p=31337 (MoT stats hub bot-blocked when checked: https://www.transport.govt.nz/statistics-and-insights/safety-annual-statistics/sheet/overseas-drivers)
